newsitem.title: UK: Brent paper stable, spot Brent heard traded lower.
newsitem.headline: Brent paper stable, spot Brent heard traded lower.

text.p: A spot cargo of Brent crude was heard traded at around the sharply lower numbers agreed in morning physical business on Friday while paper Brent values held steady in late talk, traders said.
A trading house that kept a March 17-19 loader after the five o'clock deadline was rumoured to have sold it on for around March -10 cents, equivalent to about April +20 cents.
If confirmed, that would be some five cents easier than two trades completed earlier in the day at April +25, some 30 cents below deals done on Thursday.
The cargo heard traded was one of two Brent cargoes kept from the chains on Friday. Traders heard the seller was JP Morgan but the company was not available for comment.

Earlier a Brent cargo loading March 16-18 fetched April Brent +25 cents, having been sold late on Thursday at April +35 cents. Another Brent, loading March 17-19, was kept early from the paper chains and sold on at April +25 cents.
Swiss-based trading house Glencore bought both cargoes, taking its tally for the week into double figures. It bought two March 14-16 Brents on Thursday at April Brent +55 cents.
Trade in other grades dominated afternoon physical trade, with Ekofisk and Forties changing hands at steady levels.

A Norwegian Statfjord loading March 16-18 traded at dated Brent +43 cents. An Ekofisk loading March 16-18 traded at Dated +30 cents, another loading around March 20 went at +29, while two Forties loading end March both went for Dated +42 cents.

CFDs stabilised after falling in line with the physical numbers. CFDs for next week (March 3-7) were pegged at April Brent +9/15 after a traded high of April +29 cents on Thursday. The week after was unchanged at around April +0.00/+0.07 cents.

The March/April spread held at the narrower +25/28 cent level achieved in the morning, after trading up to +51 cents on Wednesday and +30 cents on Thursday. IPE screen levels at 1831 GMT were also steady with front-month April at $19.61 a barrel.

In the Mediterranean, Urals remains offered at Dated Brent -$1, under pressure from Iraqi barrels. Further pressure emerged on Friday when refiners said Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation was offering another Kirkuk crude cargo.
Syria's state oil company Sytrol agreed a five-cent cut in the price of its heavy Souedie crude for March but is still talking to customers about Light barrels.

West African crudes remained quiet and long, with Bonny Light notionally five cents lower at Dated +45/50 and Forcados 10 cents lower at around Dated +35. Gas oil rich grades were especially vulnerable to a continuing meagre gasoil/crude crack.
"Values have got to come off a bit before any business gets done," a trader said.
